pr_body:
Fixes #7697

We need to pass the original builtin specifier (e.g. `process/browser.js` or `buffer/`) to resolve rather than just the package name (e.g. `process` or `buffer`) because the package name will resolve in node to a builtin rather than the browser version.

Thanks to @mischnic  - found the issue. Apparently [pnpm autoinstall is broken](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/8304).

Add these dev deps to your package.json. Note I was using parcel in a workspace, but these need to be installed in the project root.

```json
"buffer": "^5.5.0",
"process": "^0.11.10",
```

Then add these alias to package.json:

```json
  "alias": {
    "process": "process/browser.js",
    "buffer": "buffer"
  },
```

Then install and run parcel, and you are back working! 

also see [node emulation](https://parceljs.org/features/node-emulation/#polyfilling-%26-excluding-builtin-node-modules)

review_comments: By the way, should not this be a non-dev dependency?

Maybe? Two reasons I made it a dev dep:

1. It was a dev dependency before when it was included in Parcel itself.
2. The "process" dependency might actually be used not in your project, but by a dependency in node_modules. We cannot add the dep to that, so we add it to the project root instead. So it's kinda an indirect dependency, needed by Parcel not by your project.

I could be convinced otherwise if you feel strongly.
I was just curious, not sure if there is any difference either way.
